deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is an early draft, older than the editor's Blatt 10/11 according to his note on p.32, of the opening of Riemann's 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' / 'Gravitation und Licht' programme. Riemann lists the Newtonian hypotheses that, together with the geometric axioms, explain falling bodies and celestial motions. He does this in order to replace the bare 'force at every point' with the motion of a space-filling medium; that replacement is on p.34. The page contains no calculation, only an axiomatization. In modern notation (mine):

(H1) Law of inertia. An isolated ponderable point has x(t) = x0 + v t with v constant, possibly v = 0. Riemann remarks that this law cannot be derived from the principle of sufficient reason. Since motion is change, the persistence of motion must have a cause located in the point's own state. He then marks this argument 'Undeutlich!!' (unclear).

(H2) Any deviation from uniform rectilinear motion, i.e. any nonzero x''(t), is a change of state and requires a cause.

(H3) A change of motion is a new motion that composes vectorially with the existing one (parallelogram rule): v(t+dt) = v(t) + dv. Hence the causes, called forces, must be distinguished by magnitude and direction; they are vectors.

(H4) Field hypothesis. At every point x and time t there is a definite vector cause K(x,t), which would change the motion of any ponderable point located there.
- (4.1) The same point placed at two places suffers accelerations a1, a2 parallel to K1, K2, with |a1|:|a2| = |K1|:|K2|.
- (4.2) Hence K/a = m is a constant for a given point, differs between points, and is called its mass. So K = m a, i.e. a = K/m: Newton's second law.

(H5, misnumbered '4') The accelerating force at a place depends at each instant on the instantaneous configuration of all ponderable points.
- (5.1), continued on p.34: a single point would produce a central inverse-square force.
- Superposition then follows on p.34: K(x) = sum_i -c_i (x - x_i)/|x - x_i|^3.

On p.34 he redefines the accelerating force as the acceleration imparted equally to every resting point, which is Galilean universality of free fall.
errors: Numbering slip: the hypothesis on the dependence of force on the configuration of ponderable points is numbered '4' a second time; it should be 5.

Conceptual tension, not an algebraic error. In 4.2 the field quantity K at a place yields accelerations K/m that differ for different points. On the next page (item 3) the cause at a place gives every resting point the same acceleration (beschleunigende Kraft). For gravitation the two fit only if the 'Schwere' of the source and the response of the test body are related so that the acceleration is mass-independent. Riemann does not reconcile the two definitions on this page; the later version on Blatt 10/11 and p.34 adopts the 'accelerating force' formulation.
The argument about inertia and sufficient reason is marked 'Undeutlich!!' by Riemann himself: it is an acknowledged unclear step, not a derivation.

results.what: Axiomatic statement of Newtonian mechanics as hypotheses: inertia, deviation requires cause, parallelogram composition, force field with mass defined as force/acceleration
results.modern_name: Newton's laws of motion; operational (Machian-style) definition of inertial mass as a force/acceleration ratio
results.usually_credited_to: Newton (Principia 1687); the operational mass definition is usually associated with Mach (1868/1883)

results.what: Gravitational force at a point determined by the instantaneous configuration of all masses: inverse-square central law with vector superposition (completed on next page)
Programme of explaining the force field by the motion of a space-filling medium (announced in context)
results.modern_name: Riemann's ether theory of gravitation and light (Naturphilosophie fragments)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a preliminary draft of material already printed in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (Naturphilosophie fragments, 'Gravitation und Licht'). The content is a standard restatement of Newtonian mechanics. Minor interest: the explicit operational definition of mass as the force/acceleration quotient, and Riemann's own 'Undeutlich!!' against the sufficient-reason argument.

checkable.asserts: Uniform rectilinear motion has zero acceleration (H1).

checkable.sympy: m,a1,a2=symbols('m a1 a2',positive=True); K1=m*a1; K2=m*a2; simplify(K1/K2 - a1/a2)==0
checkable.asserts: With K = m a and fixed m, accelerations are in the ratio of the forces (4.1), and K/a is constant (4.2).
Change of motion composes with existing motion by vector addition (parallelogram rule, H3).

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,c=symbols('x y z c',positive=True); r=sqrt(x**2+y**2+z**2); F=-c*Matrix([x,y,z])/r**3; simplify(F.norm()*r**2 - c)==0
checkable.asserts: For a central inverse-square force, force times squared distance is constant (continued on p.34).

transcription_corrections: The second item labelled '4,' (beschleunigende Kraft ...) is Riemann's own misnumbering for item 5; the transcription correctly reproduces it, but it should be flagged.
'Prinzip' may be written 'Prin-zip' or 'Princip' in the image; this is orthographic only.
'Undeutlich!!' is an indented marginal-style remark by Riemann on the preceding argument, not part of the hypothesis text.
